summary: Specific notice periods apply depending on how long you've been renting and who is terminating the tenancy.
explanation: The notice period depends on how long you've been renting. For tenancies of less than 6 months, 28 days' notice is required. For 6 months to 1 year, 35 days. For 1-2 years, 42 days. For 2-3 years, 56 days. For 3-4 years, 84 days. For 4-5 years, 112 days. For 5+ years, 140 days.
compliant_examples: Proper notice period as per legislation
recommended_action: Ensure the lease specifies the correct notice period based on your tenancy duration. If it allows immediate termination, discuss this with your landlord and request the clause be amended. If they refuse, you can challenge this through the RTB.

summary: Landlords have limited rights to access the property and must give reasonable notice.
explanation: Your landlord can only enter the property for specific reasons (repairs, inspections, showing to prospective tenants) and must give you reasonable notice (usually 24 hours). They cannot enter without your permission except in emergencies.
alert_if_found: landlord can enter at any time
compliant_examples: Access only for repairs and inspections
non_compliant_examples: Landlord can enter at any time
recommended_action: Your landlord cannot enter your home without permission except in an emergency. You can politely refuse entry if they show up without giving at least 24 hours' notice. If they persist, contact the RTB.

summary: You have the right to quiet enjoyment of the property without unreasonable interference.
explanation: You have the right to live in the property without unreasonable interference from your landlord. This includes the right to privacy and to use the property as your home.
alert_if_found: landlord can interfere with quiet enjoyment
compliant_examples: Tenant has right to quiet enjoyment
non_compliant_examples: Landlord can interfere with quiet enjoyment
recommended_action: Ensure the lease respects your right to quiet enjoyment and privacy. If it allows unreasonable interference, discuss this with your landlord. Document any interference and contact the RTB if it continues.

summary: Tenancies can be terminated for serious breaches, but proper procedures must be followed.
explanation: A tenancy can be terminated for serious breaches like non-payment of rent, anti-social behavior, or damage to the property. However, proper notice and procedures must be followed.
recommended_action: Ensure the lease only allows termination for serious breaches and includes proper procedures. If it allows termination for minor issues, discuss this with your landlord and request the clause be amended.
